title: A Machine for the Orbit
premise: Bram Halloran, the last human technician aboard the automated relay station Vesper Gate, has spent a decade keeping his head down in orbits no government claims. When the deep-space freighter Calliope returns with its crew mysteriously aged backward—including Bram's presumed-dead sister Mara—the station becomes the only place that can decode the temporal anomaly they carry. But a corporate fleet is racing to seize the data, and Bram must guide the Calliope through dead space to the abandoned relay at the system's edge, where the truth about who built the anomaly—and why it chose them—finally surfaces. In the end, Bram sacrifices his own recorded identity to broadcast the cure outward, choosing justice for strangers over the self he might have reclaimed.
about_author: Ines Quintana is a former orbital logistics analyst who left the industry to write fiction about the people machines forget. She lives in Lisbon, where she repairs vintage radios and insists the future belongs to maintenance workers.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A routine cargo haul through contested orbit establishes his solitary life aboard Vesper Gate: broken coffee machine, automated voices, a decade without leave. He patches a failing antenna and reflects on the family he stopped contacting. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness beginning to curdle into something like dread.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Back Wrong
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The long-lost freighter Calliope docks unannounced, transponder dark. Its crew of twelve should be twenty years older; instead they are younger than their service records. Bram recognizes one face instantly—his sister Mara, aged backward past the day she disappeared. Emotional beat: shock cracking open old grief.

chapters.title: Mara, Unaged
chapters.summary: Alternating Bram and Mara POV. Mara remembers her disappearance as happening last week; she doesn't know Bram spent ten years mourning her. Their reunion is jagged—she grieves parents he has already buried twice. Emotional beat: love out of sync with time itself.

chapters.title: What the Calliope Carries
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The ship's black box contains an anomalous signal pattern that predates any human technology Bram knows. The crew's de-aging isn't random—it follows the signal's geometry exactly. Someone or something targeted them. Emotional beat: wonder shading into fear as patterns emerge.

chapters.title: The Company Wakes Up
chapters.summary: Station AI POV, cold and procedural. Automated systems flag the Calliope's return; ownership algorithms ping Meridian Combine, which still legally owns both vessels. A recovery fleet alters course toward Vesper Gate. Emotional beat: impersonal menace—the law itself turning hostile.

chapters.title: Crew of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The de-aged crew struggles with bodies that don't match their memories: muscle memory gone, licenses invalid, families who don't know them. One crewman, Okafor, deteriorates rapidly—the reversal isn't stable. Emotional beat: identity as something the body can revoke.

chapters.title: Invisible No Longer
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Meridian lawyers transmit a seizure order: the Calliope and everyone aboard are company property under salvage law. Bram realizes his decade of invisibility made him complicit in a system that treats people as cargo. Emotional beat: guilt igniting into defiance.

chapters.title: The Edge of Dead Space
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Old survey charts reveal Relay Nine, an abandoned station at the edge of dead space where the anomalous signal originates. It's the only place with the bandwidth to analyze the pattern before Meridian arrives. Emotional beat: a plan forming from desperation.

chapters.title: Stealing Your Own Ship
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The crew votes to run. Mara, technically junior to her own former rank, must convince her once-captain—now younger and uncertain—to let her fly. They cut the Calliope loose during a debris storm. Emotional beat: reclaiming agency across reversed hierarchies.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, aboard the Calliope now. Bram abandons Vesper Gate, his home and legal identity, riding silent through sensor-shadowed space while Meridian pursuit ships sweep behind them. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration—he is finally moving after ten static years.

chapters.title: Okafor Fading
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The reversal accelerates; he is losing memories forward and backward, forgetting his daughter's name even as his body grows stronger. He asks Mara to remember him properly if the process completes. Emotional beat: dignity dissolving, love persisting.

chapters.title: The Signal Speaks
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Decoded fragments suggest the signal is a message, not a weapon—a beacon broadcasting instructions for reversing entropy locally. Someone built it deliberately. The question becomes: for whom? Emotional beat: awe colliding with paranoia.

chapters.title: Intercepted
chapters.summary: Meridian commander Reyes's POV. Reyes boards Vesper Gate, finds Bram's quarters, and pieces together his history—including evidence Bram's original employment contract was coerced debt bondage. Reyes begins quietly doubting her employers. Emotional beat: the antagonist's conscience flickering awake.

chapters.title: Dead Space, Living Crew
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In the silence beyond the heliopause, the crew confronts what they want if reversal is possible for everyone: youth again, or the lives they already lived? Splits form between those who want to return and those who want to go forward. Emotional beat: the theme of inheritance made intimate.

chapters.title: Relay Nine
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. They reach the derelict relay and find it not abandoned but maintained—by machines running on the same signal geometry, tending equipment no human ordered kept alive. Something has been waiting here a very long time. Emotional beat: reverent unease.

chapters.title: The Builders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Bram and Mara dual POV. The relay's archives reveal the anomaly was built by a pre-collapse civilization as restitution: a machine designed to give back stolen time to those exploited by the old corporate order. Meridian's founders were among the thieves. Emotional beat: justice outside any living court.

chapters.title: Reyes Closes In
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. The Meridian fleet reaches Relay Nine's approach corridor. Ordered to fire on the relay regardless of crew casualties, Reyes stalls, buying hours—and transmitting Bram's coerced-contract evidence to an independent tribunal beacon. Emotional beat: betrayal of the corrupt in favor of the law's spirit.

chapters.title: The Choice of the Machine
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The relay can broadcast the reversal pattern system-wide—but it requires a human template, a complete recorded identity to anchor the signal. The machine offers Bram his own restoration: ten years returned, Mara's timeline matched to his. Emotional beat: temptation rendered as arithmetic.

chapters.title: What Bram Owes
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara finds Bram preparing himself as the template and begs him not to erase his identity—she just got her brother back. He argues the pattern will save thousands like Okafor. Their fight is ten years of grief finally spoken aloud. Emotional beat: love weaponized against sacrifice.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, final entry style. As Meridian weapons charge, Bram initiates the broadcast, feeding his recorded self into the signal. The reversal wave ripples outward; Okafor stabilizes; the fleet's own aging crews feel the change. Bram's memories begin to thin at the edges. Emotional beat: serene, terrifying surrender.

chapters.title: After the Wave
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The broadcast succeeds; Meridian's board faces tribunal exposure and mutinying crews. Mara holds Bram—alive but with gaps where his decade used to be—as the crew of the Calliope becomes the first witnesses in a new kind of court. Emotional beat: hard-won, imperfect justice.

chapters.title: A Machine for the Orbit
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, fragmented but hopeful. He doesn't remember the ten lost years, but Mara reads him his own logs each evening, rebuilding him by inheritance rather than memory. At Relay Nine, reactivated, he takes a new post—not hiding this time, but keeping the light on for others. Emotional beat: identity chosen anew, quiet and earned.
